summary: This bill allows dependent children under the age of 26 to be eligible for coverage under the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP) by changing the age limit from 22 to 26.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands eligibility for the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP) to include dependent children up to age 26. This expansion will likely lead to an increase in federal expenditures for these insurance programs, as more dependents will be covered.

The bill expands eligibility in the FEDVIP program by raising the dependent age limit from 22 to 26, which would increase the number of covered individuals and thereby raise federal program costs (even if premiums are primarily employee-paid). This minor spending implication makes the bill tangentially related to deficit reduction at most.
